title: Login and checkout failures
executive_summary: Login and checkout 5xx errors began at 09:29-09:30Z, about one minute after auth-service was deployed (2.13.4 to 2.14.0 at 09:28Z, which migrated JWT validation to jose-4.2 and refactored the token cache). auth-service then throws 'unsupported key type EC in JWKS' on token validation. Auth 500s propagate to api-gateway (/v1/token/verify) and payment-service (authorization checks). Error rates rose from ~0.3% to ~27% in auth, ~0.8% to ~14% in payment, and ~0.5% to ~19% in api-gateway. Latency, DB connection utilisation and timeouts were flat.

hypotheses.description: auth-service 2.14.0 deployment introduced a JWT/JWKS validation regression (jose-4.2 migration) that cannot parse EC keys, causing token validation to fail with 500s. Mechanism: After the 09:28Z deploy, JWKS validation with jose-4.2 throws TokenValidationException for EC-type keys. Auth returns 500 on token verify, so api-gateway returns 5xx on login/session checks and payment-service authorization checks fail and retry. Users are logged out when token verification fails.

probable_root_cause.label: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence)

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): deployment_regression in auth-service - auth-service 2.14.0 deployment introduced a JWT/JWKS validation regression (jose-4.2 migration) that cannot parse EC keys, causing token validation to fail with 500s.
corrective_actions: Roll back auth-service from 2.14.0 to 2.13.4 immediately (dep-cbc63772 is the trigger).
Verify recovery: auth, gateway and payment error rates return to ~0.3%, 0.5% and 0.8%.
Notify payment and checkout owners to reprocess failed authorizations from 09:29-09:40Z if needed.
preventive_actions: Add a pre-deploy test that validates JWKS containing EC keys with the jose library version in use.
Canary auth-service releases and gate them on the validation error rate.
Require a rollback plan for security-critical dependency migrations such as the JWT library.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on TokenValidationException count and auth-service 5xx rate above baseline.
Alert on the payment-service 'upstream auth-service 500' pattern.
limitations: Rollback has not been performed or verified, so causality is established by timing and error signature rather than by reversal.
Postgres and payment-service DB metrics were not queried.
Logs truncated (16 more records omitted), though the pattern summaries cover the full set.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The most likely root cause is the auth-service 2.14.0 deployment at 09:28Z. Its jose-4.2 JWT/JWKS validation fails on EC keys, which produces auth 500s. These errors cascade to api-gateway and payment-service from 09:29-09:30Z, matching the reported login and checkout failures. Rollback to 2.13.4 is the recommended action. The fix is not yet confirmed as a result of rollback.
